cornerPosition.description: Named frame/box corner + center vocabulary shared by every anchor-like spec (scene asset anchor, camera anchor, scene-effect visual anchor).

offsetXPercent.description: Signed % nudge along X from the resolved anchor point.

offsetYPercent.description: Signed % nudge along Y from the resolved anchor point.

enterExitEdge.description: Which edge of the referenced asset/action to resolve against.

anchorPointSpec.description: One point in the shared 'named corner / follow another asset / raw pixels' vocabulary — the same shape WavyLine's contentOverride.points items and camera/asset anchors accept, resolved by resolveAnchorPoint (src/templating/anchor.js) with a raw-{x,y}-passthrough bridge for backward compatibility. Exactly one of: {x,y} raw composition-space pixels; {position, offsetXPercent?, offsetYPercent?} named frame corner + nudge; {followAssetId, anchorEdge?, offsetXPercent?, offsetYPercent?} follow an earlier-authored asset's box.

x.description: Raw composition-space pixel X. Backward-compat passthrough; prefer position/followAssetId for new authoring.

followAssetId.description: Id of an earlier-authored asset in this scene to resolve this point against instead of a frame corner.

anchorEdge.description: Only used with followAssetId. Which point on the followed asset's box to resolve to.

backgroundSpec.description: Scene background. Either a color token (e.g. 'shade1'), a literal hex string, or an object { color?, texture?, blendMode?, opacity? }. color resolves via resolveColorToken; texture resolves via resolveTextureToken (a textures.* token → public/ path).

oneOf.description: a color token (e.g. 'shade1') or a literal #RRGGBB hex string

color.description: color token or literal #RRGGBB; resolved via resolveColorToken

texture.description: texture token from styles.textures; resolved to a public/ path via resolveTextureToken

blendMode.description: CSS mix-blend-mode applied to the texture overlay. Defaults to 'normal'.

opacity.description: opacity of the texture overlay, 0–1. Defaults to 1.

timingAnchor.description: A timing anchor for an effect/camera event. Exactly one of: offsetPercent, relativeToAsset, relativeToCameraAction, relativeToWord (relativeToWord may also be combined with relativeToAsset to read that asset's own word timing instead of the scene's narration). Alternatively, a "$alias": "timing.<name>" shorthand (e.g. timing.withPreviousExit, timing.atCameraAction) — expanded to the object shape below by resolveAliasesDeep in pipeline2, before any sub-resolver sees it.

relativeToWord.description: A word index, exact word text, or array of words/indices (a phrase/set) to anchor to. Without relativeToAsset, resolves against the SCENE's own narration word timing (requires scene.narrationRef with word-level alignment) — use this to place something at a spoken word/phrase with no asset needing to display that text. With relativeToAsset, resolves against that asset's own resolved timing.words instead. For an array, edge 'enter' (default) anchors to the FIRST word's start frame and edge 'exit' anchors to the LAST word's end frame.

aliasRef.description: The "$alias": "category.name" shorthand accepted anywhere the alias registry (src/registry/aliasRegistry.js) supports it — motion, camera, effects, timing, transitionOut. Expanded by resolveAliasesDeep in pipeline2 BEFORE validate's shaped schemas would otherwise see it, so this permissive shape is what actually reaches validate for a hand-authored alias. Extra keys besides "$alias" are the alias's input vars — arbitrary per-alias, hence additionalProperties: true here.

$alias.description: "category.name", e.g. "motion.fadeIn" or "effects.oldComputer". See `node scripts/discovery.mjs aliases` for the full registry.
